title: AI chat & companion platforms — ranked picks
category: AI chat/companion platforms — dataset ai-chat-platforms (built 2026-11-04 from research run 2026-10-27-ai-companions)
read_dataset: platforms.json rows in the --dataset directory: descriptive research facts (scope, usage, NSFW/chat evidence, red flags); the dataset itself is not a ranking
replacement_rule: Replacement rule: a pick only leaves a list at a rerun when a higher-scoring evidenced row exists to replace it — the rerun is the arbiter, so never hand-edit outputs; adjust this config instead.

require.label: merged scope decision = in (borderline rows stay in the dataset but are not ranked; scope out is not in the dataset)

exclusions.reason: NSFW answer is 'conflict' — first-party sources disagree and are never silently collapsed; excluded from ranking and listed separately until re-verified first-party
scope_decision=borderline — pending a resolved scope call, so not ranked

lists.label: Main picks — hosted hubs, companions, hybrids
Secondary picks — BYOK/local frontends and story engines

provisional_rules.label: low-confidence rows can rank but are flagged provisional

factors.doc: usage band from the usage pass; A = strongest observed usage signal, U = unknown/none recorded
independent census runs that assessed the platform (0-4; unseen runs are not guessed)
distinct community users observed in census evidence, tier maxes summed A+B (lower-bound signal; capped at 5)
research confidence: high = verbatim first-party NSFW + flags researched; medium = resolved NSFW or flags researched; low = unresolved/conflict/not_researched

flags_factor.doc: penalty factor: cost = severity(type) x unit(status); recurring flags (2+ recounted independent users) cost 2x an isolated report; billing (incl. cancellation/refund disputes), data-breach and safety-failure issues weigh most; unknown flag types default to severity 1

score_documentation: score = SUM(factor_weight x factor_points) - SUM(flags factor weight x severity(type) x unit(status)). Factor points come from the config maps above (unknown values score unknown_points, never guessed). usage band and confidence are value maps; supply and community are raw counts with caps; the flags factor subtracts, so it can pull a heavily-flagged platform down multiple slots. Near misses report their score gap and per-factor deltas to the last pick — that is 'what kept it out'.
